question: Which among the following has the highest boiling point?
solution:
Correct Answer **__CaO__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO)** has a **highest** **boiling point.**
 
• It undergoes a process called **calcination,** where it is heated to **very high temperatures (around 2,572°C or 4,662°F)** to convert it into **calcium oxide.**
 
• However, **calcium oxide** does not boil as a pure substance at atmospheric pressure since it undergoes thermal decomposition before reaching its **boiling point.**

 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO),** also known as **quicklime or burnt lime**, is an **inorganic compound composed of calcium and oxygen**.
 
• Chemical Formula: **CaO**
 
• Molar Mass: 56.08 g/mol

**Physical Properties:**

 
• **Appearance: Calcium oxide** is a **white, caustic, crystalline solid at room temperature.**
 
• **Melting Point:** The melting point of calcium oxide is approximately **2,572°C (4,662°F)**, indicating its solid state at normal conditions.
 
• **Boiling Point: Calcium oxide **does not have a distinct boiling point because it undergoes thermal decomposition before reaching its boiling point.
 
• When heated,** calcium oxide **decomposes into** calcium hydroxide** and releases **oxygen gas.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Cacl₂:**

 
• **Calcium chloride (CaCl₂)** is a compound that has a **relatively high boiling point** compared to many other common substances.
 
• **Calcium chloride (CaCl2**) is an inorganic compound composed of** calcium and chloride ions.**
 
• It is commonly used in various industrial, commercial, and scientific applications.

**Physical Properties:**

 
• **Appearance:** Calcium chloride is typically a white crystalline solid.
 
• **Melting Point:** The melting point of calcium chloride is around **772°C (1422°F)**, indicating its solid state at room temperature.
 
• **Boiling Point:** The boiling point of calcium chloride is approximately **1,935°C (3,515°F),** which is relatively high compared to many other substances.
 
• **Solubility: **Calcium chloride is highly soluble in water, and it forms a clear, colorless solution.
 
• The solubility of calcium chloride increases with increasing temperature.

**Nacl:**

 
• **Sodium chloride (**NaCl) is a common compound that is widely known as table salt. Here are some details about sodium chloride:
 
• **Chemical Formula: **NaCl
 
• **Molar Mass: **58.44 g/mol

**Physical Properties:**

 
• **Appearance: **Sodium chloride is a crystalline solid that is typically white or colorless.
 
• Melting Point: The melting point of sodium chloride is approximately **801°C (1,474°F).**
 
• This is the temperature at which it transitions from a solid to a liquid state.
 
• **Boiling Point: **The boiling point of sodium chloride is approximately **1,413°C (2,575°F).**
 
• This is the temperature at which it transitions from a liquid to a gaseous state.
